props.title: Three walls just fell — that's why this is worth your hour

cards.head: Construction got cheap
cards.body: Building a graph from messy wikis and code used to need a team of analysts. A language model now extracts the entities and links in an afternoon.

cards.head: Agents hit a wall
cards.body: Everyone shipped chatbots; everyone learned a model with no world just makes things up. A graph is the grounding that fixes it.

cards.head: The standards landed
cards.body: GQL became an ISO standard in 2024. GraphRAG, MCP and SHACL are production-ready today — not research toys.

props.foot: For a decade this was a rich-company secret. The tooling finally reached the rest of us.
Meaning → memory → live senses → the body → the acting mind. Build it bottom-up.

props.title: Ontology
props.sub: the layer of meaning — a shared grammar machines can agree on

props.title: Not a schema. Not a taxonomy. A model of meaning.

left.head: Schema / taxonomy
rows: A database schema says how bytes are stored.
A taxonomy is just a tree of categories.
Neither one tells a machine what a thing MEANS.
Change the storage, and the meaning is lost.

right.head: Ontology
rows: Defines entities: Report, Query, Table, Service.
Defines rules: every Report must use ≥1 Query.
Independent of any one database or vendor.

props.foot: The ontology is the contract every source, every query, and every agent shares.

props.title: Everything reduces to a triple: subject → predicate → object
props.foot: Millions of triples, sharing one vocabulary, become a graph of meaning.

props.kicker: OWL SAYS WHAT IS · SHACL SAYS WHAT MUST BE
props.title: Meaning you can reason on, and rules you can enforce
props.caption: OWL declares the concepts · SHACL validates every instance against the rules
props.foot: Machine-checkable meaning: the ontology can catch a broken model before an agent ever sees it.

props.kicker: REASONING · FACTS YOU NEVER WROTE DOWN
props.title: OWL lets the machine derive new truths from stated ones
props.foot: Declare the rules once; the reasoner keeps the derived facts correct for free.

props.title: The standards and tools you'll actually reach for
props.foot: Standards for portability; a good editor for the humans; a platform when you scale.
Each silo keeps its home; the graph just adds the connective tissue between them.
Match on keys and context, collapse the duplicates — meaning stays consistent everywhere.

props.title: Why grounding an LLM on a graph beats grounding it on text chunks
props.note: Microsoft Research — accuracy on multi-hop enterprise questions
props.foot: Structured retrieval finds the PATH, not just similar-sounding paragraphs.
A model that mirrors reality now — not a diagram someone drew last quarter.

props.title: Twins climb from ‘what is’ to ‘act on its own’
props.foot: Most teams live on rungs one and two. The top rung is where agents plug in.
Simulate the blast radius on the twin, instead of discovering it in production at 2 a.m.
Uber ETAs, Pinterest recs, fraud rings, drug discovery — all learned on graph structure.
The graph is the agent's memory, its senses, and its list of safe things to do.
Creativity from the model, guarantees from the graph — together, that's trustworthy AI.
Retrieve on the graph, reason over the path, act through a governed tool. That's the whole video.
One coherent stack — every layer earns its place, and the agent sees all of it.

props.title: You build one layer at a time — each is useful on its own

steps.label: Model the ontology
steps.sub: 20 core entities and their links — the shared words for your domain

steps.label: Build the graph
steps.sub: wire 2–3 sources, resolve entities, ship one multi-hop query

steps.label: Make it live
steps.sub: stream telemetry into node state — now it's a twin

props.foot: Each step ships value before the next one starts. Never a two-year moonshot.

props.title: The living map in one breath
props.closer: Give your machines a world — and they'll stop guessing, and start knowing.
items: Ontology = meaning: the shared grammar of entities, relations, and rules.
Knowledge graph = memory: the ontology filled with resolved, real instances.
Digital twin = live senses: the graph synced to reality, able to simulate.
Graph engineering = the body: building, validating, querying, learning at scale.
Agentic engineering = the mind: retrieve, reason, and act — grounded and governed.
Build bottom-up on your own sources; each layer ships value before the next.
